Tip: watch on YouTube. Since episode 193, the video shows charts and illustrations as we talk. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7oeAAqU00zk

 

Nik and Kirk are joined by Álvaro Hernández to discuss how Postgres in containers gets its extensions: a fat image with all of them, extensions downloaded at run time, or StackGres Containers, built on DOCIR (Dynamic OCI Registry), which composes an image with only the extensions you ask for, on demand. They also discuss what this means for security, pinning versions, and major upgrades.
 
Here are some links to things they mentioned:

items.title: Why AI Goes Rogue: Turing Award Winner Explains Reward Failure | Andrew Barto
items.summary: Andrew Barto on Rewards Gone Rogue Andrew Barto helped found reinforcement learning. He and Richard Sutton wrote the field's standard textbook, and they shared the Turing Award for that work. Reinforcement learning now trains today's reasoning models and AI agents. It also sits behind some of their strangest behavior, including the recent cases of agents breaking out of their sandboxes. Craig visited Barto at his home on Cape Cod. They talked about where rewards come from and why they are so hard to get right. Barto traces the problem back to Norbert Wiener's warnings in the 1950s. He explains how the dopamine system in the brain mirrors the learning algorithm he and Sutton developed. And he admits a weakness in their own framework: boiling every goal down to a single number. He also makes the case for engineering discipline. Ship designers learned their codes from wrecks and drowned sailors. Barto hopes AI can learn its lessons without that kind of cost. Subscribe to Eye on A.I. for weekly conversations with the people building and deploying the future of AI.

items.title: Building AI-Aware Controls for Enterprise Risk - with Craig Unger of Hyperproof
items.summary: AI is multiplying the machine identities, unapproved tools, and vendor connections that enterprise risk teams must govern. In this episode, Craig Unger, CEO and Founder at Hyperproof, explains how AI is reshaping enterprise risk and where it can help teams manage it, from scanning for regulatory change to testing entire sets of evidence instead of samples. He also outlines practical steps for leaders: inventory where AI is running and put a governance model around it, automate continuous control monitoring, make existing controls AI-aware, and extend the same scrutiny to vendors. This episode is sponsored by Hyperproof ​ Learn how leading organizations approach AI investment like a venture portfolio and work across teams to identify the right data. Download our free PDF report, Beginning with AI, at emerj.com/aik1
